1	# Playthrough Strategy
2	
3	Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
4	its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
5	area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.
6	
7	## General Strategy
8	
9	- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.
10	
11	## Recruiting Units
12	
13	In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.
14	
15	The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.
16	
17	## Promoting Units
18	
19	Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.
20	
21	In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general. Alternatively, you could give that knight crest to a cavalier, who would then use it to be promoted to a paladin. The complete promotion-item mapping is below.
22	
23	| item              | eligible classes → promoted class                                                                    |
24	| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
25	| **hero crest**    | mercenary → hero; myrmidon → swordmaster; fighter → warrior                                          |
26	| **knight crest**  | cavalier → paladin; knight → general                                                                 |
27	| **orion's bolt**  | archer → sniper; nomad → nomad trooper                                                               |
28	| **elysian whip**  | pegasus knight → falcoknight; wyvern rider → wyvern lord                                             |
29	| **guiding ring**  | mage → sage; shaman → druid; monk → bishop; cleric → bishop; troubadour → valkyrie                   |
30	| **ocean seal**    | pirate → berserker                                                                                   |
31	| **fell contract** | thief → assassin                                                                                     |
32	| **earth seal**    | any class eligible for a hero crest, knight crest, orion's bolt, elysian whip, or guiding ring       |
33	| **heaven seal**   | lyn → blade lord; eliwood → knight lord; hector → great lord, subject to story-specific restrictions |
34	
35	## Broad strategy notes
36	
37	Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.
38	
39	- (s01, Ch21) Fog chapters: a hidden enemy cannot be targeted until one of our units has moved near it and WAITED; reveal first, attack second. Ballistae are not in fe7_threat; an archer on one hits anything 3-10 tiles away.
40	- (s01, Ch21) fe7_act 'trade' fails to SWAP when both inventories are full (nothing changes hands); route the item through a unit with a free slot. 'supply' is not wired in the tool. The Merch menu can be driven by hand (it shows up as 'Merch').
41	- (s01, Ch21) A boss with a bow equipped cannot counter in melee; check fe7_forecast every turn, since his equipped weapon can change.
42	- (s02, Ch22) Item IDs: 0x25 Halberd is an AXE (Hector/fighters), 0x1B Horseslayer is the LANCE. Counters use the first usable weapon in inventory, so put the right weapon in slot 0 with a fe7_forecast weapon_slot (it re-equips) before ending a turn on the front line. Note that a forecast re-equips even when cancelled, so check slot 0 again before a committed attack.
43	- (s02, Ch22) Weapons are scarce and there is no shop or healer yet: track uses and route spares through trades early.
44	- (s03, Ch23) The Prep screen's Trade -> Items menu (Trd/Use/Trnsfr/List/Sell/Give all) reaches BENCHED units, so spare weapons and stat/promotion items can be moved and Used there. Yes/No prompts default to No; press Left before A.
45	- (s03, Ch23) If the chapter can end during an enemy/green phase, fe7_wait will press through the ending, the next chapter's opening AND its Prep screen (Start = Fight), and its A on an "inventory full" prompt sends the equipped weapon to the convoy. Near the end of a chapter, poll with fe7_unstick instead of fe7_wait.
46	- (s04, Ch24) Before trusting a turn-1 board, check whether the map is FOGGED: a hazy screen plus enemies that do not render. fe7_threat still lists hidden enemies, but an attack refuses (the menu shows only Item/Wait) until a unit has waited within about 3 tiles. fe7_threat ignores ballistae: check the screenshot for ballista sprites.
47	- (s04, Ch24) Enemy AI byte at unit +0x44: 0x03 means it waits until you enter its move+range, then attacks; 0x00/0x0D/0x0F means it advances. A boss with 0x03 can be lured onto a tile of your choosing: leave it exactly one legal attack tile next to a tank.
48	- (s05, Ch25) If an objective is unclear, read the chapter's event data in ROM instead of guessing: search ROM for the first enemy's 16-byte unit entry (char, class, 00, flags, x, y, x, y, items, AI), search for that address as a pointer to find the chapter's event header, and read its misc-event list. Code 0x0B entries are AREA events (flag, script ptr, x1 y1 x2 y2): a unit has to WAIT on those tiles. The Prep-screen opening (skipped with Start) is where objectives like "points" are explained.
49	- (s05, Ch25) A General with Def 19+ and a lance is untouchable by cavaliers, pegasi, monks, archers and ballistae: park him alone in a choke as bait and let his counters do the killing. Watch his lance uses; the Horseslayer broke mid-chapter.
50	- (s06, Ch26) Turn-event reinforcements are in ROM: event header pointer [0] -> 16-byte entries (02 00 00 00, script ptr, start turn, end turn, .., mode byte at +0xC: 1/2 Eliwood N/H, 3/4 Hector N/H). Each script is "32 00 00 00 <unit list ptr>", 16-byte units. Item table names: 0x2C-0x33 are bows (Iron, Steel, Silver, Poison, Killer, Brave, Short, Long), 0x37 Fire, 0x38 Thunder, 0x39 Elfire, 0x3F Shine, 0x40 Divine, 0x44 Flux, 0x45 Luna, 0x4D Physic, 0x95 Short Spear, 0x6C Elixir.
51	- (s06, Ch26) The prep "List" screen moves an item straight from its owner to the selected unit. Fliers rescue and then canto across peaks, which makes a two-turn ferry that keeps lords and dancers out of reach. In FE7, bows do x2 Mt against fliers.
52	- (s07, Ch27) Item IDs: 0x69 Door Key, 0x6A Lockpick, 0x6F Torch, 0x6D Pure Water, 0x78 Chest Key (5 uses), 0x79 Mine, 0x7A Light Rune, 0x73 White Gem, 0x75 Red Gem, 0x3A Bolting. Item table at 0x08BE222C, 36 bytes per item (+0x14 uses, +0x19 range, +0x1E use effect). Units shown standing on "Roof" with state 0x81 are hidden inside a building until its door is opened.
53	- (s07, Ch27) fe7_act staff (and sometimes forecast/trade from a unit acting in place) fails with "action menu could not be located"; staff by hand works. Misses do not consume weapon uses. fe7_wait's "nothing changed" can miss enemy moves — re-read fe7_state each turn.
54	
55	## Lyn mode

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general. content.content:
`0x0202A5B4` also names the **highlighted menu entry**, not just map contents. Observed on
Lyn Ch.7:

| State | Buffer reads |
|---|---|
| field menu just opened (A on empty ground) | `"End."` |
| a unit's action menu just opened | `"Wait"` |
| after backing out to the map | `"Defeat Heintz."` — the OBJECTIVE |

Two consequences.

**The objective IS readable from memory** (`"Defeat Heintz."`), so a `fe7_objective` tool needs
no new research — only a rule for when the buffer is showing it. It is state-dependent, not
absent; an earlier session caught `"Seize gate"` the same way at a turn boundary.

**⚠️ The field menu opens with End Turn ALREADY HIGHLIGHTED.** The buffer read `"End."` the

Useful as a cheap "can I drive the cursor right now?" probe. **Inferred** — it held across
several transitions but the mechanism isn't understood.

### `0x0202521B` — a real toggle, but NOT a general "modal open" flag

It reliably toggles `0 → 1 → 0`, but it does **not** mean what I first concluded. Observed:

| State | `0x0202521B` |
|---|---|
| Free cursor on the map | `0` |
| `Start` → objective window open | **`1`** |
| `A` on a unit → selection | **`1`** |
| **`A` on empty tile → field menu open** | **`0`** ← breaks the theory |

The field-menu case is decisive: `0x0202517C` read `count=5, index=1, state=1` (unambiguously
open, and `Down` moved its index instead of the cursor) while this flag sat at `0`.

**Do not use it as an "is map input live?" test.** Its actual semantics are unknown — it may
track a unit-info//full-screen panel rather than modality. Recorded as **Unverified**.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general. Alternatively, you could give that knight crest to a cavalier, who would then use it to be promoted to a paladin. The complete promotion-item mapping is below.

| item              | eligible classes → promoted class                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **hero crest**    | mercenary → hero; myrmidon → swordmaster; fighter → warrior                                          |
| **knight crest**  | cavalier → paladin; knight → general                                                                 |
| **orion's bolt**  | archer → sniper; nomad → nomad trooper                                                               |
| **elysian whip**  | pegasus knight → falcoknight; wyvern rider → wyvern lord                                             |
| **guiding ring**  | mage → sage; shaman → druid; monk → bishop; cleric → bishop; troubadour → valkyrie                   |
| **ocean seal**    | pirate → berserker                                                                                   |
| **fell contract** | thief → assassin                                                                                     |
| **earth seal**    | any class eligible for a hero crest, knight crest, orion's bolt, elysian whip, or guiding ring       |
| **heaven seal**   | lyn → blade lord; eliwood → knight lord; hector → great lord, subject to story-specific restrictions |

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- (s01, Ch21) Fog chapters: a hidden enemy cannot be targeted until one of our units has moved near it and WAITED; reveal first, attack second. Ballistae are not in fe7_threat; an archer on one hits anything 3-10 tiles away.
- (s01, Ch21) fe7_act 'trade' fails to SWAP when both inventories are full (nothing changes hands); route the item through a unit with a free slot. 'supply' is not wired in the tool. The Merch menu can be driven by hand (it shows up as 'Merch').
- (s01, Ch21) A boss with a bow equipped cannot counter in melee; check fe7_forecast every turn, since his equipped weapon can change.
- (s02, Ch22) Item IDs: 0x25 Halberd is an AXE (Hector/fighters), 0x1B Horseslayer is the LANCE. Counters use the first usable weapon in inventory, so put the right weapon in slot 0 with a fe7_forecast weapon_slot (it re-equips) before ending a turn on the front line. Note that a forecast re-equips even when cancelled, so check slot 0 again before a committed attack.
- (s02, Ch22) Weapons are scarce and there is no shop or healer yet: track uses and route spares through trades early.
- (s03, Ch23) The Prep screen's Trade -> Items menu (Trd/Use/Trnsfr/List/Sell/Give all) reaches BENCHED units, so spare weapons and stat/promotion items can be moved and Used there. Yes/No prompts default to No; press Left before A.
- (s03, Ch23) If the chapter can end during an enemy/green phase, fe7_wait will press through the ending, the next chapter's opening AND its Prep screen (Start = Fight), and its A on an "inventory full" prompt sends the equipped weapon to the convoy. Near the end of a chapter, poll with fe7_unstick instead of fe7_wait.
- (s04, Ch24) Before trusting a turn-1 board, check whether the map is FOGGED: a hazy screen plus enemies that do not render. fe7_threat still lists hidden enemies, but an attack refuses (the menu shows only Item/Wait) until a unit has waited within about 3 tiles. fe7_threat ignores ballistae: check the screenshot for ballista sprites.
- (s04, Ch24) Enemy AI byte at unit +0x44: 0x03 means it waits until you enter its move+range, then attacks; 0x00/0x0D/0x0F means it advances. A boss with 0x03 can be lured onto a tile of your choosing: leave it exactly one legal attack tile next to a tank.
- (s05, Ch25) If an objective is unclear, read the chapter's event data in ROM instead of guessing: search ROM for the first enemy's 16-byte unit entry (char, class, 00, flags, x, y, x, y, items, AI), search for that address as a pointer to find the chapter's event header, and read its misc-event list. Code 0x0B entries are AREA events (flag, script ptr, x1 y1 x2 y2): a unit has to WAIT on those tiles. The Prep-screen opening (skipped with Start) is where objectives like "points" are explained.
- (s05, Ch25) A General with Def 19+ and a lance is untouchable by cavaliers, pegasi, monks, archers and ballistae: park him alone in a choke as bait and let his counters do the killing. Watch his lance uses; the Horseslayer broke mid-chapter.
- (s06, Ch26) Turn-event reinforcements are in ROM: event header pointer [0] -> 16-byte entries (02 00 00 00, script ptr, start turn, end turn, .., mode byte at +0xC: 1/2 Eliwood N/H, 3/4 Hector N/H). Item table at 0x08BE222C, 36 bytes per item (+0x14 uses, +0x19 range, +0x1E use effect). Units shown standing on "Roof" with state 0x81 are hidden inside a building until its door is opened.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general. Alternatively, you could give that knight crest to a cavalier, who would then use it to be promoted to a paladin. The complete promotion-item mapping is below.

| item              | eligible classes → promoted class                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **hero crest**    | mercenary → hero; myrmidon → swordmaster; fighter → warrior                                          |
| **knight crest**  | cavalier → paladin; knight → general                                                                 |
| **orion's bolt**  | archer → sniper; nomad → nomad trooper                                                               |
| **elysian whip**  | pegasus knight → falcoknight; wyvern rider → wyvern lord                                             |
| **guiding ring**  | mage → sage; shaman → druid; monk → bishop; cleric → bishop; troubadour → valkyrie                   |
| **ocean seal**    | pirate → berserker                                                                                   |
| **fell contract** | thief → assassin                                                                                     |
| **earth seal**    | any class eligible for a hero crest, knight crest, orion's bolt, elysian whip, or guiding ring       |
| **heaven seal**   | lyn → blade lord; eliwood → knight lord; hector → great lord, subject to story-specific restrictions |

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- (s01, Ch21) Fog chapters: a hidden enemy cannot be targeted until one of our units has moved near it and WAITED; reveal first, attack second. Ballistae are not in fe7_threat; an archer on one hits anything 3-10 tiles away.
- (s01, Ch21) fe7_act 'trade' fails to SWAP when both inventories are full (nothing changes hands); route the item through a unit with a free slot. 'supply' is not wired in the tool. The Merch menu can be driven by hand (it shows up as 'Merch').
- (s01, Ch21) A boss with a bow equipped cannot counter in melee; check fe7_forecast every turn, since his equipped weapon can change.
- (s02, Ch22) Item IDs: 0x25 Halberd is an AXE (Hector/fighters), 0x1B Horseslayer is the LANCE. Counters use the first usable weapon in inventory, so put the right weapon in slot 0 with a fe7_forecast weapon_slot (it re-equips) before ending a turn on the front line. Note that a forecast re-equips even when cancelled, so check slot 0 again before a committed attack.
- (s02, Ch22) Weapons are scarce and there is no shop or healer yet: track uses and route spares through trades early.
- (s03, Ch23) The Prep screen's Trade -> Items menu (Trd/Use/Trnsfr/List/Sell/Give all) reaches BENCHED units, so spare weapons and stat/promotion items can be moved and Used there. Yes/No prompts default to No; press Left before A.
- (s03, Ch23) If the chapter can end during an enemy/green phase, fe7_wait will press through the ending, the next chapter's opening AND its Prep screen (Start = Fight), and its A on an "inventory full" prompt sends the equipped weapon to the convoy. Near the end of a chapter, poll with fe7_unstick instead of fe7_wait.
- (s04, Ch24) Before trusting a turn-1 board, check whether the map is FOGGED: a hazy screen plus enemies that do not render. fe7_threat still lists hidden enemies, but an attack refuses (the menu shows only Item/Wait) until a unit has waited within about 3 tiles. fe7_threat ignores ballistae: check the screenshot for ballista sprites.
- (s04, Ch24) Enemy AI byte at unit +0x44: 0x03 means it waits until you enter its move+range, then attacks; 0x00/0x0D/0x0F means it advances. A boss with 0x03 can be lured onto a tile of your choosing: leave it exactly one legal attack tile next to a tank.
- (s05, Ch25) If an objective is unclear, read the chapter's event data in ROM instead of guessing: search ROM for the first enemy's 16-byte unit entry (char, class, 00, flags, x, y, x, y, items, AI), search for that address as a pointer to find the chapter's event header, and read its misc-event list. Code 0x0B entries are AREA events (flag, script ptr, x1 y1 x2 y2): a unit has to WAIT on those tiles. The Prep-screen opening (skipped with Start) is where objectives like "points" are explained.
- (s05, Ch25) A General with Def 19+ and a lance is untouchable by cavaliers, pegasi, monks, archers and ballistae: park him alone in a choke as bait and let his counters do the killing. Watch his lance uses; the Horseslayer broke mid-chapter.
- (s06, Ch26) Turn-event reinforcements are in ROM: event header pointer [0] -> 16-byte entries (02 00 00 00, script ptr, start turn, end turn, .., mode byte at +0xC: 1/2 Eliwood N/H, 3/4 Hector N/H). Each script is "32 00 00 00 <unit list ptr>", 16-byte units. Item table names: 0x2C-0x33 are bows (Iron, Steel, Silver, Poison, Killer, Brave, Short, Long), 0x37 Fire, 0x38 Thunder, 0x39 Elfire, 0x3F Shine, 0x40 Divine, 0x44 Flux, 0x45 Luna, 0x4D Physic, 0x95 Short Spear, 0x6C Elixir.
- (s06, Ch26) The prep "List" screen moves an item straight from its owner to the selected unit. Fliers rescue and then canto across peaks, which makes a two-turn ferry that keeps lords and dancers out of reach. In FE7, bows do x2 Mt against fliers.
- (s07, Ch27) Item IDs: 0x69 Door Key, 0x6A Lockpick, 0x6F Torch, 0x6D Pure Water, 0x78 Chest Key (5 uses), 0x79 Mine, 0x7A Light Rune, 0x73 White Gem, 0x75 Red Gem, 0x3A Bolting. Item table at 0x08BE222C, 36 bytes per item (+0x14 uses, +0x19 range, +0x1E use effect). Units shown standing on "Roof" with state 0x81 are hidden inside a building until its door is opened.
- (s07, Ch27) fe7_act staff (and sometimes forecast/trade from a unit acting in place) fails with "action menu could not be located"; staff by hand works. Misses do not consume weapon uses. fe7_wait's "nothing changed" can miss enemy moves — re-read fe7_state each turn.

content.content:
The page gives only a partial account of protecting Zephiel, and it doesn't include exact coordinates, door locations, or a full turn-by-turn log.

**Starting setup**
- The army begins in the northern courtyard and splits in two. Eliwood's group (excluding Dart) heads east. Hector, Priscilla, and Harken, plus the units with them, head west.
- Zephiel starts unconscious in his room. Nobody is assigned to guard him at the start.
- A thief is recommended in each group, since a thief is needed to open doors and to steal back treasure.

**Zephiel's behaviour**
- After the first turn he wakes up. He considers running, then decides that running would let enemies surround him, so he stays and fights.
- He moves onto a Pillar, which gives him 20 extra Avoid. The author says he should still not be made to fight much because his stats are weak and his Silver Sword slows him.
- The chapter ends once he survives 15 turns.

**How enemies approached**
- Ursula is positioned south of the area and is not close enough to threaten Jaffar at the start.
- Maxime rushes Jaffar, not Zephiel.
- A swordslayer guards the east side near the doors and targets the thief who opens them.
- Enemy mages and archers can swamp Jaffar when he leaves his Pillar, which the author notes is a risk.

**Route and key turns**
- **Turn 5:** Nino is reached. Eliwood's group talks with her and persuades her to leave the Black Fang.
- **Turn 10:** Jaffar and Nino are brought together. Jaffar agrees to fight with the group.
- **Around this point:** Heath rescues Hector and pulls him out of Ursula's range. Eliwood goes to Zephiel's room and talks with him. Zephiel decides to trust Eliwood and places his life in their hands.
- **After round 3:** Canas kills Ursula, which ends the chapter's main fighting.

**Not covered:** The page does not describe exact unit positions around Zephiel's room, which doors were opened when, or a complete turn-by-turn record of the defense.

content.content:
The page gives a route for this chapter but doesn't say how Zephiel behaves or whether he sits on a pillar, so I can't cover those.

**Setup**
- **Objective:** Protect Zephiel for 15 turns. Ursula is the boss.
- **Units:** You can field 14 units. Nino joins if Eliwood talks to him.
- **Enemies:** The start has many mages, mercenaries, knights, and other units. Reinforcements include shamans, a general, and a thief.

**Route**
1. **Split into two groups.**
   - *Left group:* Two high-movement units and a thief.
   - *Right group:* At least one high-movement unit and Eliwood.

2. **Left group:**
   - Open the door with the thief or a Door Key.
   - Send one high-movement unit to rescue Jaffar and bring him right so Nino can talk to him. This unlocks the side quest (chapter 26X), but only if Nino talks to Jaffar before the chapter ends.
   - Send the other high-movement unit with the thief to the locked door. An enemy thief should appear there. Kill him before he steals the chests.
   - Take the treasure with the thief or a chest key.
   - Afterward, carry the thief to the treasure room on the right side.

3. **Right group:**
   - Open the door with a thief or Door Key, or wait for the enemy to open it.
   - Move a high-movement unit to the locked door quickly. Block the enemy thief's escape, then have your thief steal the item and finish him off.
   - Move Eliwood next to Nino to recruit him.
   - Move a strong unit to guard Zephiel.

**Boss: Ursula**
- She has very high resistance but doesn't move.
- If you have Pegasus Knights or Falcon Knights, they make the fight easy.
- Otherwise, place a high-resistance unit next to her so she uses up her Bolting attacks on that unit, then attack her.

**Reward:** Finishing the chapter gives you the second Heaven Seal.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general. Alternatively, you could give that knight crest to a cavalier, who would then use it to be promoted to a paladin. The complete promotion-item mapping is below.

| item              | eligible classes → promoted class                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **hero crest**    | mercenary → hero; myrmidon → swordmaster; fighter → warrior                                          |
| **knight crest**  | cavalier → paladin; knight → general                                                                 |
| **orion's bolt**  | archer → sniper; nomad → nomad trooper                                                               |
| **elysian whip**  | pegasus knight → falcoknight; wyvern rider → wyvern lord                                             |
| **guiding ring**  | mage → sage; shaman → druid; monk → bishop; cleric → bishop; troubadour → valkyrie                   |
| **ocean seal**    | pirate → berserker                                                                                   |
| **fell contract** | thief → assassin                                                                                     |
| **earth seal**    | any class eligible for a hero crest, knight crest, orion's bolt, elysian whip, or guiding ring       |
| **heaven seal**   | lyn → blade lord; eliwood → knight lord; hector → great lord, subject to story-specific restrictions |

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- (s01, Ch21) Fog chapters: a hidden enemy cannot be targeted until one of our units has moved near it and WAITED; reveal first, attack second. Ballistae are not in fe7_threat; an archer on one hits anything 3-10 tiles away.
- (s01, Ch21) fe7_act 'trade' fails to SWAP when both inventories are full (nothing changes hands); route the item through a unit with a free slot. 'supply' is not wired in the tool. The Merch menu can be driven by hand (it shows up as 'Merch').
- (s01, Ch21) A boss with a bow equipped cannot counter in melee; check fe7_forecast every turn, since his equipped weapon can change.
- (s02, Ch22) Item IDs: 0x25 Halberd is an AXE (Hector/fighters), 0x1B Horseslayer is the LANCE. Counters use the first usable weapon in inventory, so put the right weapon in slot 0 with a fe7_forecast weapon_slot (it re-equips) before ending a turn on the front line. Note that a forecast re-equips even when cancelled, so check slot 0 again before a committed attack.
- (s02, Ch22) Weapons are scarce and there is no shop or healer yet: track uses and route spares through trades early.
- (s03, Ch23) The Prep screen's Trade -> Items menu (Trd/Use/Trnsfr/List/Sell/Give all) reaches BENCHED units, so spare weapons and stat/promotion items can be moved and Used there. Yes/No prompts default to No; press Left before A.
- (s03, Ch23) If the chapter can end during an enemy/green phase, fe7_wait will press through the ending, the next chapter's opening AND its Prep screen (Start = Fight), and its A on an "inventory full" prompt sends the equipped weapon to the convoy. Near the end of a chapter, poll with fe7_unstick instead of fe7_wait.
- (s04, Ch24) Before trusting a turn-1 board, check whether the map is FOGGED: a hazy screen plus enemies that do not render. fe7_threat still lists hidden enemies, but an attack refuses (the menu shows only Item/Wait) until a unit has waited within about 3 tiles. fe7_threat ignores ballistae: check the screenshot for ballista sprites.
- (s04, Ch24) Enemy AI byte at unit +0x44: 0x03 means it waits until you enter its move+range, then attacks; 0x00/0x0D/0x0F means it advances. A boss with 0x03 can be lured onto a tile of your choosing: leave it exactly one legal attack tile next to a tank.
- (s05, Ch25) If an objective is unclear, read the chapter's event data in ROM instead of guessing: search ROM for the first enemy's 16-byte unit entry (char, class, 00, flags, x, y, x, y, items, AI), search for that address as a pointer to find the chapter's event header, and read its misc-event list. Code 0x0B entries are AREA events (flag, script ptr, x1 y1 x2 y2): a unit has to WAIT on those tiles. The Prep-screen opening (skipped with Start) is where objectives like "points" are explained.
- (s05, Ch25) A General with Def 19+ and a lance is untouchable by cavaliers, pegasi, monks, archers and ballistae: park him alone in a choke as bait and let his counters do the killing. Watch his lance uses; the Horseslayer broke mid-chapter.
- (s06, Ch26) Turn-event reinforcements are in ROM: event header pointer [0] -> 16-byte entries (02 00 00 00, script ptr, start turn, end turn, .., mode byte at +0xC: 1/2 Eliwood N/H, 3/4 Hector N/H). Each script is "32 00 00 00 <unit list ptr>", 16-byte units. Item table names: 0x2C-0x33 are bows (Iron, Steel, Silver, Poison, Killer, Brave, Short, Long), 0x37 Fire, 0x38 Thunder, 0x39 Elfire, 0x3F Shine, 0x40 Divine, 0x44 Flux, 0x45 Luna, 0x4D Physic, 0x95 Short Spear, 0x6C Elixir.
- (s06, Ch26) The prep "List" screen moves an item straight from its owner to the selected unit. Fliers rescue and then canto across peaks, which makes a two-turn ferry that keeps lords and dancers out of reach. In FE7, bows do x2 Mt against fliers.
- (s07, Ch27) Item IDs: 0x69 Door Key, 0x6A Lockpick, 0x6F Torch, 0x6D Pure Water, 0x78 Chest Key (5 uses), 0x79 Mine, 0x7A Light Rune, 0x73 White Gem, 0x75 Red Gem, 0x3A Bolting. Item table at 0x08BE222C, 36 bytes per item (+0x14 uses, +0x19 range, +0x1E use effect). Units shown standing on "Roof" with state 0x81 are hidden inside a building until its door is opened.
- (s07, Ch27) fe7_act staff (and sometimes forecast/trade from a unit acting in place) fails with "action menu could not be located"; staff by hand works. Misses do not consume weapon uses. fe7_wait's "nothing changed" can miss enemy moves — re-read fe7_state each turn.

**Objectives:**

"Defeat enemy" — rout, 38 enemies at the start ("Left 38" on the map). Snowy town map 25x26, SNOW WEATHER: movement costs are roughly x3 for everyone (the game's grid for an enemy cavalier was 12 tiles vs 33 in fe7_threat), so fe7_threat badly OVER-states ranges here; use `verify`. We start in the SW pocket (x0-6, y16-25), which only opens north (x0-1) and east along row 16. 17 enemies stand on Roof tiles with state flag 0x81 (hidden; not drawn on the map), incl. the boss-like ch59 (Light Brand) at (21,1). Each building opens with a DOOR KEY (item 0x69, use effect 0x1F) used from its stairs: (16,21)/(16,22), (23,17)/(23,18), (21,5)/(21,6) boss, (5,14)/(5,15), (14,3)/(14,4). # Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general. Alternatively, you could give that knight crest to a cavalier, who would then use it to be promoted to a paladin. The complete promotion-item mapping is below.

| item              | eligible classes → promoted class                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **hero crest**    | mercenary → hero; myrmidon → swordmaster; fighter → warrior                                          |
| **knight crest**  | cavalier → paladin; knight → general                                                                 |
| **orion's bolt**  | archer → sniper; nomad → nomad trooper                                                               |
| **elysian whip**  | pegasus knight → falcoknight; wyvern rider → wyvern lord                                             |
| **guiding ring**  | mage → sage; shaman → druid; monk → bishop; cleric → bishop; troubadour → valkyrie                   |
| **ocean seal**    | pirate → berserker                                                                                   |
| **fell contract** | thief → assassin                                                                                     |
| **earth seal**    | any class eligible for a hero crest, knight crest, orion's bolt, elysian whip, or guiding ring       |
| **heaven seal**   | lyn → blade lord; eliwood → knight lord; hector → great lord, subject to story-specific restrictions |

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- (s01, Ch21) Fog chapters: a hidden enemy cannot be targeted until one of our units has moved near it and WAITED; reveal first, attack second. Ballistae are not in fe7_threat; an archer on one hits anything 3-10 tiles away.
- (s01, Ch21) fe7_act 'trade' fails to SWAP when both inventories are full (nothing changes hands); route the item through a unit with a free slot. 'supply' is not wired in the tool. The Merch menu can be driven by hand (it shows up as 'Merch').
- (s01, Ch21) A boss with a bow equipped cannot counter in melee; check fe7_forecast every turn, since his equipped weapon can change.
- (s02, Ch22) Item IDs: 0x25 Halberd is an AXE (Hector/fighters), 0x1B Horseslayer is the LANCE. Counters use the first usable weapon in inventory, so put the right weapon in slot 0 with a fe7_forecast weapon_slot (it re-equips) before ending a turn on the front line. Note that a forecast re-equips even when cancelled, so check slot 0 again before a committed attack.
- (s02, Ch22) Weapons are scarce and there is no shop or healer yet: track uses and route spares through trades early.
- (s03, Ch23) The Prep screen's Trade -> Items menu (Trd/Use/Trnsfr/List/Sell/Give all) reaches BENCHED units, so spare weapons and stat/promotion items can be moved and Used there. Yes/No prompts default to No; press Left before A.
- (s03, Ch23) If the chapter can end during an enemy/green phase, fe7_wait will press through the ending, the next chapter's opening AND its Prep screen (Start = Fight), and its A on an "inventory full" prompt sends the equipped weapon to the convoy. Near the end of a chapter, poll with fe7_unstick instead of fe7_wait.
- (s04, Ch24) Before trusting a turn-1 board, check whether the map is FOGGED: a hazy screen plus enemies that do not render. fe7_threat still lists hidden enemies, but an attack refuses (the menu shows only Item/Wait) until a unit has waited within about 3 tiles. fe7_threat ignores ballistae: check the screenshot for ballista sprites.
- (s04, Ch24) Enemy AI byte at unit +0x44: 0x03 means it waits until you enter its move+range, then attacks; 0x00/0x0D/0x0F means it advances. A boss with 0x03 can be lured onto a tile of your choosing: leave it exactly one legal attack tile next to a tank.
- (s05, Ch25) If an objective is unclear, read the chapter's event data in ROM instead of guessing: search ROM for the first enemy's 16-byte unit entry (char, class, 00, flags, x, y, x, y, items, AI), search for that address as a pointer to find the chapter's event header, and read its misc-event list. Code 0x0B entries are AREA events (flag, script ptr, x1 y1 x2 y2): a unit has to WAIT on those tiles. The Prep-screen opening (skipped with Start) is where objectives like "points" are explained.
- (s05, Ch25) A General with Def 19+ and a lance is untouchable by cavaliers, pegasi, monks, archers and ballistae: park him alone in a choke as bait and let his counters do the killing. Watch his lance uses; the Horseslayer broke mid-chapter.
- (s06, Ch26) Turn-event reinforcements are in ROM: event header pointer [0] -> 16-byte entries (02 00 00 00, script ptr, start turn, end turn, .., mode byte at +0xC: 1/2 Eliwood N/H, 3/4 Hector N/H). Each script is "32 00 00 00 <unit list ptr>", 16-byte units. Item table names: 0x2C-0x33 are bows (Iron, Steel, Silver, Poison, Killer, Brave, Short, Long), 0x37 Fire, 0x38 Thunder, 0x39 Elfire, 0x3F Shine, 0x40 Divine, 0x44 Flux, 0x45 Luna, 0x4D Physic, 0x95 Short Spear, 0x6C Elixir.
- (s06, Ch26) The prep "List" screen moves an item straight from its owner to the selected unit. Fliers rescue and then canto across peaks, which makes a two-turn ferry that keeps lords and dancers out of reach. In FE7, bows do x2 Mt against fliers.
- (s07, Ch27) Item IDs: 0x69 Door Key, 0x6A Lockpick, 0x6F Torch, 0x6D Pure Water, 0x78 Chest Key (5 uses), 0x79 Mine, 0x7A Light Rune, 0x73 White Gem, 0x75 Red Gem, 0x3A Bolting. Item table at 0x08BE222C, 36 bytes per item (+0x14 uses, +0x19 range, +0x1E use effect). Units shown standing on "Roof" with state 0x81 are hidden inside a building until its door is opened.
- (s07, Ch27) fe7_act staff (and sometimes forecast/trade from a unit acting in place) fails with "action menu could not be located"; staff by hand works. Misses do not consume weapon uses. fe7_wait's "nothing changed" can miss enemy moves — re-read fe7_state each turn.

**s08, attempt 2: LOST on turn 6 again** (Zephiel at full HP on PP6 was swarmed on EP6 off-pillar at (13,13), the same tile and turn as attempt 1). Healing between phases does not stop a 4-6 attacker burst. Notes: the convoy holds 2 Door Keys (take them at prep, Trnsfr->Take). Turn 4's player phase was SKIPPED after fe7_end_turn on turn 3 (tool/game glitch). Guides say Zephiel normally stands on a pillar (+20 avoid) and that players also lose him to swarms and restart. The east chests are (21,13) Rescue staff and (22,14) Delphi Shield; the west ones are Boots and Brave Lance.

+**s08, attempt 3: LOST on turn 10** (Zephiel swarmed by 6 enemies inside his room on EP10, at full HP after Physic). The Prep screen was skipped by an extra queued Start press (default deployment, no trades): press Start ONE at a time during the opening and screenshot after each. Jaffar SURVIVED EP2 this time (RNG), plugged the room entrance and killed ~5 enemies until his Killing Edge broke (turn 8); that alone kept Zephiel alive 4 turns longer. Door opened turn 3 (Pent killed the key fighter from (19,5) on T2; Rath took the key at (19,4), rode 8 to (26,5) on T3). The boss at (28,26) has Bolting (3-10) and never moves before turn 13: never end a turn within 10 tiles of it, except Oswin as a sponge. The hall route reaches the room entrance on turn 10 at best; by then the entrance (13-14,18-20) is clogged.

+- PLAN for attempt 4: Rescue staff in the (21,13) chest (room x20-23 y13-15, door (21,16), stairs (21,17) from the hall). Give Pent a convoy Door Key and Heath's Chest Key at prep, and take him south with the army: door ~T8, chest ~T9, then Rescue Zephiel out to Pent's side (from (21,14) Zephiel's pillars are about 6 away). Physic also reaches the room from there.

- PLAN for attempt 2: Pent's Physic range is Mag/2 = 9. From the courtyard's south edge, (13-15,6), he reaches Zephiel's room (e.g. (14,6)->(14,14) = 8) through the walls. Keep Pent there all chapter and heal Zephiel every turn. Push everyone else east for Nino.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general. Alternatively, you could give that knight crest to a cavalier, who would then use it to be promoted to a paladin. The complete promotion-item mapping is below.

| item              | eligible classes → promoted class                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **hero crest**    | mercenary → hero; myrmidon → swordmaster; fighter → warrior                                          |
| **knight crest**  | cavalier → paladin; knight → general                                                                 |
| **orion's bolt**  | archer → sniper; nomad → nomad trooper                                                               |
| **elysian whip**  | pegasus knight → falcoknight; wyvern rider → wyvern lord                                             |
| **guiding ring**  | mage → sage; shaman → druid; monk → bishop; cleric → bishop; troubadour → valkyrie                   |
| **ocean seal**    | pirate → berserker                                                                                   |
| **fell contract** | thief → assassin                                                                                     |
| **earth seal**    | any class eligible for a hero crest, knight crest, orion's bolt, elysian whip, or guiding ring       |
| **heaven seal**   | lyn → blade lord; eliwood → knight lord; hector → great lord, subject to story-specific restrictions |

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- (s01, Ch21) Fog chapters: a hidden enemy cannot be targeted until one of our units has moved near it and WAITED; reveal first, attack second. Ballistae are not in fe7_threat; an archer on one hits anything 3-10 tiles away.
- (s01, Ch21) fe7_act 'trade' fails to SWAP when both inventories are full (nothing changes hands); route the item through a unit with a free slot. 'supply' is not wired in the tool. The Merch menu can be driven by hand (it shows up as 'Merch').
- (s01, Ch21) A boss with a bow equipped cannot counter in melee; check fe7_forecast every turn, since his equipped weapon can change.
- (s02, Ch22) Item IDs: 0x25 Halberd is an AXE (Hector/fighters), 0x1B Horseslayer is the LANCE. Counters use the first usable weapon in inventory, so put the right weapon in slot 0 with a fe7_forecast weapon_slot (it re-equips) before ending a turn on the front line. Note that a forecast re-equips even when cancelled, so check slot 0 again before a committed attack.
- (s02, Ch22) Weapons are scarce and there is no shop or healer yet: track uses and route spares through trades early.
- (s03, Ch23) The Prep screen's Trade -> Items menu (Trd/Use/Trnsfr/List/Sell/Give all) reaches BENCHED units, so spare weapons and stat/promotion items can be moved and Used there. Yes/No prompts default to No; press Left before A.
- (s03, Ch23) If the chapter can end during an enemy/green phase, fe7_wait will press through the ending, the next chapter's opening AND its Prep screen (Start = Fight), and its A on an "inventory full" prompt sends the equipped weapon to the convoy. Near the end of a chapter, poll with fe7_unstick instead of fe7_wait.
- (s04, Ch24) Before trusting a turn-1 board, check whether the map is FOGGED: a hazy screen plus enemies that do not render. fe7_threat still lists hidden enemies, but an attack refuses (the menu shows only Item/Wait) until a unit has waited within about 3 tiles. fe7_threat ignores ballistae: check the screenshot for ballista sprites.
- (s04, Ch24) Enemy AI byte at unit +0x44: 0x03 means it waits until you enter its move+range, then attacks; 0x00/0x0D/0x0F means it advances. A boss with 0x03 can be lured onto a tile of your choosing: leave it exactly one legal attack tile next to a tank.
- (s05, Ch25) If an objective is unclear, read the chapter's event data in ROM instead of guessing: search ROM for the first enemy's 16-byte unit entry (char, class, 00, flags, x, y, x, y, items, AI), search for that address as a pointer to find the chapter's event header, and read its misc-event list. Code 0x0B entries are AREA events (flag, script ptr, x1 y1 x2 y2): a unit has to WAIT on those tiles. The Prep-screen opening (skipped with Start) is where objectives like "points" are explained.
- (s05, Ch25) A General with Def 19+ and a lance is untouchable by cavaliers, pegasi, monks, archers and ballistae: park him alone in a choke as bait and let his counters do the killing. Watch his lance uses; the Horseslayer broke mid-chapter.
- (s06, Ch26) Turn-event reinforcements are in ROM: event header pointer [0] -> 16-byte entries (02 00 00 00, script ptr, start turn, end turn, .., mode byte at +0xC: 1/2 Eliwood N/H, 3/4 Hector N/H). Each script is "32 00 00 00 <unit list ptr>", 16-byte units. Item table names: 0x2C-0x33 are bows (Iron, Steel, Silver, Poison, Killer, Brave, Short, Long), 0x37 Fire, 0x38 Thunder, 0x39 Elfire, 0x3F Shine, 0x40 Divine, 0x44 Flux, 0x45 Luna, 0x4D Physic, 0x95 Short Spear, 0x6C Elixir.
- (s06, Ch26) The prep "List" screen moves an item straight from its owner to the selected unit. Fliers rescue and then canto across peaks, which makes a two-turn ferry that keeps lords and dancers out of reach. In FE7, bows do x2 Mt against fliers.
- (s07, Ch27) Item IDs: 0x69 Door Key, 0x6A Lockpick, 0x6F Torch, 0x6D Pure Water, 0x78 Chest Key (5 uses), 0x79 Mine, 0x7A Light Rune, 0x73 White Gem, 0x75 Red Gem, 0x3A Bolting. Item table at 0x08BE222C, 36 bytes per item (+0x14 uses, +0x19 range, +0x1E use effect). Units shown standing on "Roof" with state 0x81 are hidden inside a building until its door is opened.
- (s07, Ch27) fe7_act staff (and sometimes forecast/trade from a unit acting in place) fails with "action menu could not be located"; staff by hand works. Misses do not consume weapon uses. fe7_wait's "nothing changed" can miss enemy moves — re-read fe7_state each turn.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general. Alternatively, you could give that knight crest to a cavalier, who would then use it to be promoted to a paladin. The complete promotion-item mapping is below.

| item              | eligible classes → promoted class                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **hero crest**    | mercenary → hero; myrmidon → swordmaster; fighter → warrior                                          |
| **knight crest**  | cavalier → paladin; knight → general                                                                 |
| **orion's bolt**  | archer → sniper; nomad → nomad trooper                                                               |
| **elysian whip**  | pegasus knight → falcoknight; wyvern rider → wyvern lord                                             |
| **guiding ring**  | mage → sage; shaman → druid; monk → bishop; cleric → bishop; troubadour → valkyrie                   |
| **ocean seal**    | pirate → berserker                                                                                   |
| **fell contract** | thief → assassin                                                                                     |
| **earth seal**    | any class eligible for a hero crest, knight crest, orion's bolt, elysian whip, or guiding ring       |
| **heaven seal**   | lyn → blade lord; eliwood → knight lord; hector → great lord, subject to story-specific restrictions |

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- (s01, Ch21) Fog chapters: a hidden enemy cannot be targeted until one of our units has moved near it and WAITED; reveal first, attack second. Ballistae are not in fe7_threat; an archer on one hits anything 3-10 tiles away.
- (s01, Ch21) fe7_act 'trade' fails to SWAP when both inventories are full (nothing changes hands); route the item through a unit with a free slot. 'supply' is not wired in the tool. The Merch menu can be driven by hand (it shows up as 'Merch').
- (s01, Ch21) A boss with a bow equipped cannot counter in melee; check fe7_forecast every turn, since his equipped weapon can change.
- (s02, Ch22) Item IDs: 0x25 Halberd is an AXE (Hector/fighters), 0x1B Horseslayer is the LANCE. Counters use the first usable weapon in inventory, so put the right weapon in slot 0 with a fe7_forecast weapon_slot (it re-equips) before ending a turn on the front line. Note that a forecast re-equips even when cancelled, so check slot 0 again before a committed attack.
- (s02, Ch22) Weapons are scarce and there is no shop or healer yet: track uses and route spares through trades early.
- (s03, Ch23) The Prep screen's Trade -> Items menu (Trd/Use/Trnsfr/List/Sell/Give all) reaches BENCHED units, so spare weapons and stat/promotion items can be moved and Used there. Yes/No prompts default to No; press Left before A.
- (s03, Ch23) If the chapter can end during an enemy/green phase, fe7_wait will press through the ending, the next chapter's opening AND its Prep screen (Start = Fight), and its A on an "inventory full" prompt sends the equipped weapon to the convoy. Near the end of a chapter, poll with fe7_unstick instead of fe7_wait.
- (s04, Ch24) Before trusting a turn-1 board, check whether the map is FOGGED: a hazy screen plus enemies that do not render. fe7_threat still lists hidden enemies, but an attack refuses (the menu shows only Item/Wait) until a unit has waited within about 3 tiles. fe7_threat ignores ballistae: check the screenshot for ballista sprites.
- (s04, Ch24) Enemy AI byte at unit +0x44: 0x03 means it waits until you enter its move+range, then attacks; 0x00/0x0D/0x0F means it advances. A boss with 0x03 can be lured onto a tile of your choosing: leave it exactly one legal attack tile next to a tank.
- (s05, Ch25) If an objective is unclear, read the chapter's event data in ROM instead of guessing: search ROM for the first enemy's 16-byte unit entry (char, class, 00, flags, x, y, x, y, items, AI), search for that address as a pointer to find the chapter's event header, and read its misc-event list. Code 0x0B entries are AREA events (flag, script ptr, x1 y1 x2 y2): a unit has to WAIT on those tiles. The Prep-screen opening (skipped with Start) is where objectives like "points" are explained.
- (s05, Ch25) A General with Def 19+ and a lance is untouchable by cavaliers, pegasi, monks, archers and ballistae: park him alone in a choke as bait and let his counters do the killing. Watch his lance uses; the Horseslayer broke mid-chapter.
- (s06, Ch26) Turn-event reinforcements are in ROM: event header pointer [0] -> 16-byte entries (02 00 00 00, script ptr, start turn, end turn, .., mode byte at +0xC: 1/2 Eliwood N/H, 3/4 Hector N/H). Each script is "32 00 00 00 <unit list ptr>", 16-byte units. Item table names: 0x2C-0x33 are bows (Iron, Steel, Silver, Poison, Killer, Brave, Short, Long), 0x37 Fire, 0x38 Thunder, 0x39 Elfire, 0x3F Shine, 0x40 Divine, 0x44 Flux, 0x45 Luna, 0x4D Physic, 0x95 Short Spear, 0x6C Elixir.
- (s06, Ch26) The prep "List" screen moves an item straight from its owner to the selected unit. Fliers rescue and then canto across peaks, which makes a two-turn ferry that keeps lords and dancers out of reach. In FE7, bows do x2 Mt against fliers.
- (s07, Ch27) Item IDs: 0x69 Door Key, 0x6A Lockpick, 0x6F Torch, 0x6D Pure Water, 0x78 Chest Key (5 uses), 0x79 Mine, 0x7A Light Rune, 0x73 White Gem, 0x75 Red Gem, 0x3A Bolting. Item table at 0x08BE222C, 36 bytes per item (+0x14 uses, +0x19 range, +0x1E use effect). Units shown standing on "Roof" with state 0x81 are hidden inside a building until its door is opened.
- (s07, Ch27) fe7_act staff (and sometimes forecast/trade from a unit acting in place) fails with "action menu could not be located"; staff by hand works. Misses do not consume weapon uses. fe7_wait's "nothing changed" can miss enemy moves — re-read fe7_state each turn.

A 3-HP Guy on the house at (2,15) died. Also Lv15 myrmidons (Silver Sword / Steel Blade) and cls39 axe units arrive in the north from turn 3-4.
- Both monks sit on forts (+avoid): three of my four attacks on a 2-HP monk missed. Melee them, or block the forts before turn 4 (a unit standing on a fort may stop the spawn: untested).
- Rath (19 HP) died at (4,15) to a monk plus an unexplained 13-damage hit (Canas also took 13 at (6,17)), probably the Lv15 Steel Blade myrmidon. Do not leave anyone below ~25 HP in any threat count >= 2.
- Turn 1 logistics that worked: Marcus->Canas Guiding Ring (Canas -> Druid); Heath's Javelin -> Sain; Wil supplied the Brave Axe out of Merlinus's convoy (pressing A on 'Merch' by hand, Take, axe tab) and traded it to Hector. Convoy also holds Longbow, Orion's Bolt, 2 Door Keys, Red Gem. Gold reads 0, so there is no shopping and the Arena at (2,13) is useless.
- No healer at all: the only heal was Eliwood's single Vulnerary.

**s04, attempt 2: WON on turn 5. No deaths. Wallace NOT recruited (he stays in the fog in the crowded NE, and Florina at Lv3 was too fragile to send). Geitz is 24a-only, so he was never available (Dart is dead).**
- Prep: benched Bartre, Guy, Rath, Rebecca; fielded Florina, Isadora (given Guy's Killing Edge and Kent's Steel Sword), Hawkeye (given Bartre's Hand Axe and Halberd) and Ninian. Prep Items: Canas used the Guiding Ring (now a Druid), Hector used the Secret Book (Skl 13) and took the Brave Axe from the convoy (the Hammer went in), Eliwood used Afa's Drops, Heath's Javelin went to Sain, and Wil holds the Light Rune and Longbow. The convoy still holds an Orion's Bolt. Matthew holds a Brave Bow that Wil cannot use yet.
- How it was won: T2 killed the monk (Hector) and a revealed wyvern (Marcus); the second wyvern died on Marcus's counter. T4: Oswin stood on the (7,16) fort. Lloyd acts first while the myrmidon still blocks (7,14), so (7,15) is his only attack tile and he must fight in melee. Oswin's Horseslayer counter took him 41->23 and killed the myrmidon. T5: Hector Brave-Axed the monk that spawned on the (6,15) fort, and Marcus stepped onto that fort and killed Lloyd with the Silver Sword (89%).

### Chapter 25 — Crazed Beast

**Objectives:**

"Earn 3 points." A point is scored by having any player unit **WAIT on each of the three castle gates**: NW (4,3), SW (2,17), NE (21,4). The third one ends the chapter. These are AREA events in the ROM event data (misc list at 0x08CA4734); killing the gate commanders does NOT score. Each gate sits inside a walled 3x3 castle with one entrance: (4,4), (2,18), (21,5). Gate holders: Pascal (ch57 Paladin, Spear, NW), a Warrior (Silver Axe, SW) and a Bishop (Purge 3-10, NE). Map 25x21 around a central lake; we start in a pocket at the south-centre.

**Recruits:**

**Agent notes:**

**s05: WON on attempt 1, turn 23. No deaths. Farina NOT recruited (0 gold).**
- I lost about 15 turns because I did not know what the points were (the opening was skipped at Prep). Done right, this is about a 6-8 turn chapter: send Hector/Hawkeye/Marcus to the three gates, kill each commander or lure it out, then WAIT on the gate.
- Enemies keep reinforcing until about turn 12: cavaliers from the north edge and the NW forts, pegasi from the NE edge, hammer pirates near the SW castle, monks respawning at the NE castle mouth every turn. Halberd/Hammer pirates are effective on our cavalry and on Oswin. A ballista archer at (12,4) has 10-tile range.
- What worked: turtling in the start pocket with Oswin (Def 19-22) alone in the mouth as bait (everything did 0 to him), and Hector at Def 20. Pascal (AI 0x03) walked off his gate onto Hawkeye; Hawkeye's Killer Axe and Hector's Brave Axe killed him.
- Gains: Hector Lv20, Oswin Lv5, Hawkeye Lv6, Marcus Lv15, Eliwood Lv5, Canas Lv2. Oswin picked up the Divine tome (0x40).
- Broken or used up: Hector's Brave Axe and Hand Axe, Marcus's Longsword (he has Silver Sword x2 and weapon 0x95 x6 left), Oswin's Horseslayer. Oswin now has Steel Lance x1 only; give him a lance. Eliwood's Vulnerary was drunk by Marcus. There is still no healer, and gold is 0.
- Ending: one Save screen, and I chose the slot in use (Ch.25: Crazed Beast). Handover is at the Ch.26 Prep screen ("Survive"). The game also deployed Bartre and Guy.

Map 21x27, mostly Peaks/Mountains; our start is split by a peak band (rows 13-15) into a north plaza (Hector, Eliwood, Lyn + Pent and Louise, who join at the start) and a southern basin around Merlinus's immobile tent at (12,18); a mountain ridge (x13-17) splits the basin again from the houses to the east. Vaida (ch2B, Wyvern Lord, 60 HP, Spear) sits at (17,2) with AI 0x03 and never moved; do not kill her (needed for Ch29).

**Recruits:**

None.

- Reinforcements (read from the ROM turn events; this is the Hector Hard list): wyverns arrive in fours at the map corners on turns 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7-10. Almost all carry Iron Lances (19 attack); two javelin wyverns (range 1-2) come from the SE on turns 4-5. Many hover near the castle or the west forts and never engage. Hector, alone in the north plaza at (10,9), took 0 damage all chapter and killed three on counters.

Lords and fragile units sat on tiles whose 4 neighbours were all allies, and the javelin wyverns were killed first. Every turn I ran fe7_threat and checked that no exposed unit could take more hits than its HP. Bows do x2 (not x3) against wyverns: Louise does 28-29 per hit, Wil about 14.

Wil holds the last Elixir, Louise none. Oswin has Javelin + Divine. Florina is carrying Rebecca and Heath is carrying Ninian; the game resets that at the next chapter. The convoy still has a Hammer x3; Florina and Lyn each hold a Red Gem (sell value). Gold is 0.

Snowy town map 25x26, SNOW WEATHER: movement costs are roughly x3 for everyone (the game's grid for an enemy cavalier was 12 tiles vs 33 in fe7_threat), so fe7_threat badly OVER-states ranges here; use `verify`. We start in the SW pocket (x0-6, y16-25), which only opens north (x0-1) and east along row 16. 17 enemies stand on Roof tiles with state flag 0x81 (hidden; not drawn on the map), incl. the boss-like ch59 (Light Brand) at (21,1). Keys came from 3 drops on visible units + drops of the General (16,19), Hero (23,14) and fighter (5,12) inside: exactly enough. Door opened turn 3 (Pent killed the key fighter from (19,5) on T2; Rath took the key at (19,4), rode 8 to (26,5) on T3). The boss at (28,26) has Bolting (3-10) and never moves before turn 13: never end a turn within 10 tiles of it, except Oswin as a sponge. The hall route reaches the room entrance on turn 10 at best; by then the entrance (13-14,18-20) is clogged.

35	## Broad strategy notes
36	
37	Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.
38	
39	- (s01, Ch21) Fog chapters: a hidden enemy cannot be targeted until one of our units has moved near it and WAITED; reveal first, attack second. Ballistae are not in fe7_threat; an archer on one hits anything 3-10 tiles away.
40	- (s01, Ch21) fe7_act 'trade' fails to SWAP when both inventories are full (nothing changes hands); route the item through a unit with a free slot. 'supply' is not wired in the tool. The Merch menu can be driven by hand (it shows up as 'Merch').
41	- (s01, Ch21) A boss with a bow equipped cannot counter in melee; check fe7_forecast every turn, since his equipped weapon can change.
42	- (s02, Ch22) Item IDs: 0x25 Halberd is an AXE (Hector/fighters), 0x1B Horseslayer is the LANCE. Counters use the first usable weapon in inventory, so put the right weapon in slot 0 with a fe7_forecast weapon_slot (it re-equips) before ending a turn on the front line. Note that a forecast re-equips even when cancelled, so check slot 0 again before a committed attack.
43	- (s02, Ch22) Weapons are scarce and there is no shop or healer yet: track uses and route spares through trades early.
44	- (s03, Ch23) The Prep screen's Trade -> Items menu (Trd/Use/Trnsfr/List/Sell/Give all) reaches BENCHED units, so spare weapons and stat/promotion items can be moved and Used there. Yes/No prompts default to No; press Left before A.
45	- (s03, Ch23) If the chapter can end during an enemy/green phase, fe7_wait will press through the ending, the next chapter's opening AND its Prep screen (Start = Fight), and its A on an "inventory full" prompt sends the equipped weapon to the convoy. Near the end of a chapter, poll with fe7_unstick instead of fe7_wait.
46	- (s04, Ch24) Before trusting a turn-1 board, check whether the map is FOGGED: a hazy screen plus enemies that do not render. fe7_threat still lists hidden enemies, but an attack refuses (the menu shows only Item/Wait) until a unit has waited within about 3 tiles. fe7_threat ignores ballistae: check the screenshot for ballista sprites.
47	- (s04, Ch24) Enemy AI byte at unit +0x44: 0x03 means it waits until you enter its move+range, then attacks; 0x00/0x0D/0x0F means it advances. A boss with 0x03 can be lured onto a tile of your choosing: leave it exactly one legal attack tile next to a tank.
48	- (s05, Ch25) If an objective is unclear, read the chapter's event data in ROM instead of guessing: search ROM for the first enemy's 16-byte unit entry (char, class, 00, flags, x, y, x, y, items, AI), search for that address as a pointer to find the chapter's event header, and read its misc-event list. Code 0x0B entries are AREA events (flag, script ptr, x1 y1 x2 y2): a unit has to WAIT on those tiles. The Prep-screen opening (skipped with Start) is where objectives like "points" are explained.
49	- (s05, Ch25) A General with Def 19+ and a lance is untouchable by cavaliers, pegasi, monks, archers and ballistae: park him alone in a choke as bait and let his counters do the killing. Watch his lance uses; the Horseslayer broke mid-chapter.
50	- (s06, Ch26) Turn-event reinforcements are in ROM: event header pointer [0] -> 16-byte entries (02 00 00 00, script ptr, start turn, end turn, .., mode byte at +0xC: 1/2 Eliwood N/H, 3/4 Hector N/H). Each script is "32 00 00 00 <unit list ptr>", 16-byte units. Item table names: 0x2C-0x33 are bows (Iron, Steel, Silver, Poison, Killer, Brave, Short, Long), 0x37 Fire, 0x38 Thunder, 0x39 Elfire, 0x3F Shine, 0x40 Divine, 0x44 Flux, 0x45 Luna, 0x4D Physic, 0x95 Short Spear, 0x6C Elixir.
51	- (s06, Ch26) The prep "List" screen moves an item straight from its owner to the selected unit. Fliers rescue and then canto across peaks, which makes a two-turn ferry that keeps lords and dancers out of reach. In FE7, bows do x2 Mt against fliers.
52	- (s07, Ch27) Item IDs: 0x69 Door Key, 0x6A Lockpick, 0x6F Torch, 0x6D Pure Water, 0x78 Chest Key (5 uses), 0x79 Mine, 0x7A Light Rune, 0x73 White Gem, 0x75 Red Gem, 0x3A Bolting. Item table at 0x08BE222C, 36 bytes per item (+0x14 uses, +0x19 range, +0x1E use effect). Units shown standing on "Roof" with state 0x81 are hidden inside a building until its door is opened.
53	- (s07, Ch27) fe7_act staff (and sometimes forecast/trade from a unit acting in place) fails with "action menu could not be located"; staff by hand works. Misses do not consume weapon uses. fe7_wait's "nothing changed" can miss enemy moves — re-read fe7_state each turn.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- (s01, Ch21) Fog chapters: a hidden enemy cannot be targeted until one of our units has moved near it and WAITED; reveal first, attack second. Ballistae are not in fe7_threat; an archer on one hits anything 3-10 tiles away.
- (s01, Ch21) fe7_act 'trade' fails to SWAP when both inventories are full (nothing changes hands); route the item through a unit with a free slot. 'supply' is not wired in the tool. The Merch menu can be driven by hand (it shows up as 'Merch').
- (s01, Ch21) A boss with a bow equipped cannot counter in melee; check fe7_forecast every turn, since his equipped weapon can change.
- (s02, Ch22) Item IDs: 0x25 Halberd is an AXE (Hector/fighters), 0x1B Horseslayer is the LANCE. Counters use the first usable weapon in inventory, so put the right weapon in slot 0 with a fe7_forecast weapon_slot (it re-equips) before ending a turn on the front line. Note that a forecast re-equips even when cancelled, so check slot 0 again before a committed attack.
- (s02, Ch22) Weapons are scarce and there is no shop or healer yet: track uses and route spares through trades early.
- (s03, Ch23) The Prep screen's Trade -> Items menu (Trd/Use/Trnsfr/List/Sell/Give all) reaches BENCHED units, so spare weapons and stat/promotion items can be moved and Used there. Yes/No prompts default to No; press Left before A.
- (s03, Ch23) If the chapter can end during an enemy/green phase, fe7_wait will press through the ending, the next chapter's opening AND its Prep screen (Start = Fight), and its A on an "inventory full" prompt sends the equipped weapon to the convoy. Near the end of a chapter, poll with fe7_unstick instead of fe7_wait.
- (s04, Ch24) Before trusting a turn-1 board, check whether the map is FOGGED: a hazy screen plus enemies that do not render. fe7_threat still lists hidden enemies, but an attack refuses (the menu shows only Item/Wait) until a unit has waited within about 3 tiles. fe7_threat ignores ballistae: check the screenshot for ballista sprites.
- (s04, Ch24) Enemy AI byte at unit +0x44: 0x03 means it waits until you enter its move+range, then attacks; 0x00/0x0D/0x0F means it advances. A boss with 0x03 can be lured onto a tile of your choosing: leave it exactly one legal attack tile next to a tank.
- (s05, Ch25) If an objective is unclear, read the chapter's event data in ROM instead of guessing: search ROM for the first enemy's 16-byte unit entry (char, class, 00, flags, x, y, x, y, items, AI), search for that address as a pointer to find the chapter's event header, and read its misc-event list. Code 0x0B entries are AREA events (flag, script ptr, x1 y1 x2 y2): a unit has to WAIT on those tiles. The Prep-screen opening (skipped with Start) is where objectives like "points" are explained.
- (s05, Ch25) A General with Def 19+ and a lance is untouchable by cavaliers, pegasi, monks, archers and ballistae: park him alone in a choke as bait and let his counters do the killing. Watch his lance uses; the Horseslayer broke mid-chapter.
- (s06, Ch26) Turn-event reinforcements are in ROM: event header pointer [0] -> 16-byte entries (02 00 00 00, script ptr, start turn, end turn, .., mode byte at +0xC: 1/2 Eliwood N/H, 3/4 Hector N/H). Each script is "32 00 00 00 <unit list ptr>", 16-byte units. Item table names: 0x2C-0x33 are bows (Iron, Steel, Silver, Poison, Killer, Brave, Short, Long), 0x37 Fire, 0x38 Thunder, 0x39 Elfire, 0x3F Shine, 0x40 Divine, 0x44 Flux, 0x45 Luna, 0x4D Physic, 0x95 Short Spear, 0x6C Elixir.
- (s06, Ch26) The prep "List" screen moves an item straight from its owner to the selected unit. Fliers rescue and then canto across peaks, which makes a two-turn ferry that keeps lords and dancers out of reach. In FE7, bows do x2 Mt against fliers.
- (s07, Ch27) Item IDs: 0x69 Door Key, 0x6A Lockpick, 0x6F Torch, 0x6D Pure Water, 0x78 Chest Key (5 uses), 0x79 Mine, 0x7A Light Rune, 0x73 White Gem, 0x75 Red Gem, 0x3A Bolting. Item table at 0x08BE222C, 36 bytes per item (+0x14 uses, +0x19 range, +0x1E use effect). Units shown standing on "Roof" with state 0x81 are hidden inside a building until its door is opened.
- (s07, Ch27) fe7_act staff (and sometimes forecast/trade from a unit acting in place) fails with "action menu could not be located"; staff by hand works. Misses do not consume weapon uses. fe7_wait's "nothing changed" can miss enemy moves — re-read fe7_state each turn.
